median_after_tax_household_income_2020_c.source: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census of Population, Focus on Geography Series / key indicators
median_after_tax_household_income_2020_c.note: Published in 2020 constant dollars. Convert to current dollars with CPI 18-10-0005 before comparing to PUMF current-dollar medians.

unaffordable_housing_stir_ge_30_percent.source: Statistics Canada, The Daily, 21 September 2022; 2021 Census key indicators
unaffordable_housing_stir_ge_30_percent.definition: Share of households spending 30% or more of income on shelter. Official Census unaffordable-housing rate uses before-tax income; universe is owner/renter non-farm non-reserve private households with income > 0 and STIR < 100%.

core_housing_need.source: Statistics Canada / CMHC core housing need; 2016 Census CHN table; The Daily 21 September 2022
core_housing_need.note: Core housing need is not residual-income hardship. Used only as an independent housing-affordability benchmark.

cmhc_housing_hardship.source: CMHC Research Insight, Introducing the Housing Hardship Concept, January 2020 (catalogue-style PDF 69619)
cmhc_housing_hardship.definition: Household is in housing hardship if residual income (disposable income after housing costs) is below the non-shelter portion of the MBM. Square-root equivalence. Regional MBM. Disposable income is the MBM disposable-income concept, not Census TOTINC_AT. Universe: private non-farm non-band non-reserve households with positive disposable income; negative residual income excluded; households with investment/capital-gain/farm income or equivalized income above the provincial median cannot be classified as in hardship.

published_rates_cis.note: Canadian Income Survey, not Census PUMF. STIR>30% in the same publication is about 11% (before-tax, restricted universe).

census_2021_update.title: New insights on affordability: update on housing hardship from the 2021 Census (NH18-33/85-2024E-PDF)
census_2021_update.status: PDF listed at publications.gc.ca; retrieval timed out / file later removed (25 Nov 2025). Canada-wide 2021 Census official hardship rate not independently recovered in this reconstruction.

private_households.source: Statistics Canada Census / NHS household counts; 2016 hierarchical PUMF The Daily 18 June 2019
private_households.note: 2016 hierarchical PUMF is a 1% sample of 14,072,079 private households (The Daily reported 140,705 HH / 343,330 persons in the PUMF).

low_income_mbm_persons.source: Statistics Canada, Income in Canada 2020 / 2021 Census
low_income_mbm_persons.note: Person-level official poverty (MBM), not household residual-income hardship.
